properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 18 at 2:30PM PST until November 18 at 5:30PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
FFWMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Timber burn area...

* Until 530 PM PST.

* At 230 PM PST, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain falling over the Timber Burn Area. Between 1 and 2
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to
0.75 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow moving through the Drainages within
Lafler, Castro and Graves Canyons, as well as drainages between
Grimes and Castro Canyons. The debris flow can consist of rock,
mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Timber Burn Area.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Timber Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los Padres National Forecast from
Andrew Molera State Park to Partington Ridge including the town of
Big Sur.
properties.instruction:
Move away from recently burned areas. Life-threatening flooding of
creeks, and roads is likely. The heavy rains will likely trigger
rockslides, mudslides, and debris flows in steep terrain. Impacted
areas include locations along Highway 1 near mile marker 50 south of
Andrew Molera State Park to mile maker 38. Other areas impacted
include Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park Campground and Partington Ridge,
structures along the Big Sur River, Mule Creek Canyon, and adjacent
drainages and watershed outlets.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 5:30 PM PST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 5:30 PM PST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued November 18 at 7:05PM PST until November 18 at 8:30PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
FFWMTR

The National Weather Service in San Francisco has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Timber burn area in...
Western Monterey County in central California...

* Until 830 PM PST.

* At 705 PM PST, CHP has reported an observed debris flow into NB
Highway One lanes in the vicinity of Big Sur Lodge and boulders in
the roadway at Hurricane Point. A car was reported stuck in the
debris flow near Big Sur. Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated that heavy rain was falling over the Timber Burn Area.
Between 3 and 6 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall
rate is 0.5 to 0.75 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts
of 1 to 3 inches are possible in the warned area. Conditions remain
favorable for additional moderate to heavy rainfall due to
orographic lift as the main rainband exits the county. Flash
flooding is ongoing. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will
result in debris flow moving through the Drainages within Lafler,
Castro and Graves Canyons, as well as drainages between Grimes and
Castro Canyons. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding in and around the Timber Burn Area.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Timber Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los Padres National Forecast from
Andrew Molera State Park to Partington Ridge including the town of
Big Sur.

At 5:43 PM PST CHP reported a debris flow across NB Highway 1 lanes
in the vicinity of Big Sur Lodge. One hour rain rates have crossed
0.7" with additional heavy rain expected this evening into tomorrow
as scattered showers with the potential for moderate to heavy rain
and thunderstorms. CHP additionally reported boulders in the NB lane
of Highway One at Hurricane Point at 6:11 PM local time. CHP reported
a car stuck in the debris flow at Big Sur.
